overview.title: Start a defensible MFRM analysis
overview.summary: Move from a research question to checked data, a fitted model, bounded interpretation, and a reviewable report.
overview.prerequisites: State the study question and what one row, one score, and each facet represent. A fitted result is not required to use this guide.
overview.computed: When requested, the application checks input structure, fits the selected model, and organizes available evidence with limitations and next checks.
overview.can_show: It can show whether requested evidence is available and where interpretation can continue or should pause.
overview.cannot_show: Completing the workflow cannot establish validity, fairness, or suitability for a decision.
overview.next_check: Before estimation, confirm data roles and design coverage. After estimation, begin with First read.
overview.next_action: Choose the next incomplete task: prepare data, review design, run estimation, interpret evidence, or prepare a report.
overview.safe_report: We followed the stated model, design checks, and interpretation limits for this analysis.
overview.avoid_report: The application confirmed that the assessment is valid.
overview.search_alias: getting started; analysis workflow; first steps; safe interpretation

overview.title: The analysis path
overview.body: Work in four stages: define the question, prepare and check the design, estimate the model, then interpret and report only the evidence that is available.

shortest_path.title: Shortest safe path
shortest_path.body: Map Person, Score, and facet columns; review missingness and connectedness; run estimation; read the first-result checks; then open only the detail needed for the research question.

claim_boundaries.title: Keep claims within the evidence
claim_boundaries.body: A completed run is a workflow event, not a validity finding. Preserve cautions, unavailable checks, uncertainty, and design limits whenever results are summarized.

long_format.title: Prepare long-format rating data
long_format.summary: Organize one observed rating per row so persons, scores, and facet elements retain their study meaning.
long_format.prerequisites: Know the observational unit, the score scale, and which design factors are facets.
long_format.computed: The input review counts rows, recognizes mapped roles, and identifies missing required values; it does not infer the intended study design.
long_format.can_show: It can show whether rows contain the roles required for the requested analysis.
long_format.cannot_show: Correct table shape does not demonstrate data quality, representativeness, or design validity.
long_format.next_check: Inspect several rows and confirm that repeated persons and facet elements reflect actual observations rather than duplicated records.
long_format.next_action: Reshape the data so each row represents one rating and each required role has its own column.
long_format.safe_report: The analysis used long-format records with one observed rating per row.
long_format.avoid_report: The data were valid because they were accepted by the application.
long_format.search_alias: long data; one rating per row; input layout; delimiter

overview.title: Why long format is required
overview.body: Long format preserves the link among a person, a score, and every facet element involved in that observed rating. This link is needed to estimate facet effects.

row_meaning.title: Define what one row means
row_meaning.body: One row should describe one observed scoring event. If several rubric criteria are separate ratings, store them as separate rows or model them according to the stated design.

required_columns.title: Required roles
required_columns.body: Provide a Person column, an ordered Score column, and the facet columns needed by the study, such as item, task, criterion, or rater. Identifiers should be consistent within each role.

missingness.title: Missing values in long data
missingness.body: A missing score is not a zero. Keep structurally absent ratings distinguishable from recorded scores, and review missing identifiers before estimation.

mapping.title: Map columns to analysis roles
mapping.summary: Tell the application which columns identify persons, scores, and each facet without changing their substantive meaning.
mapping.prerequisites: Use a long-format table and know the role of every column selected for analysis.
mapping.computed: The mapping check verifies required roles and summarizes the values assigned to each role.
mapping.can_show: It can show whether the selected columns are structurally usable for the requested model.
mapping.cannot_show: A successful mapping does not show that the design, construct, or scoring process is appropriate.
mapping.next_check: Compare the mapped role labels with several source rows and verify score ordering and facet identifiers.
mapping.next_action: Correct any swapped, duplicated, or omitted role before running estimation.
mapping.safe_report: Person, Score, and facet roles were mapped according to the stated scoring design.
mapping.avoid_report: The column mapping verified the measurement design.
mapping.search_alias: column roles; person column; score column; facet mapping

overview.title: Mapping preserves meaning
overview.body: Mapping assigns an analysis role to an existing column. It should reflect the study design rather than whichever column name looks most similar.

roles.title: Person, Score, and facet roles
roles.body: Person identifies the object being measured, Score contains ordered rating categories, and each facet identifies a systematic design condition to estimate.

check_mapping.title: Check before running
check_mapping.body: Confirm that Person values recur as expected, scores use the intended ordered categories, and each selected facet contains the intended elements rather than labels from another role.

missingness.title: Review missing and excluded observations
missingness.summary: Distinguish planned absence from unexpected missingness and document which observations enter estimation.
missingness.prerequisites: Know which person-by-facet observations were possible or assigned under the study design.
missingness.computed: The data audit counts missing required values and observations excluded by input rules.
missingness.can_show: It can show where recorded data are absent and how many rows remain available for estimation.
missingness.cannot_show: Observed missingness patterns alone cannot establish why values are missing or whether missingness is ignorable.
missingness.next_check: Compare missingness by person and facet with assignment records, administration conditions, and scoring procedures.
missingness.next_action: Correct recording errors, document planned absence, and reconsider claims that rely on poorly observed groups or elements.
missingness.safe_report: We report the observed missingness pattern, exclusions, and the design context used to interpret them.
missingness.avoid_report: Missing values were random because the overall percentage was small.
missingness.search_alias: missing data; excluded rows; planned missingness; data audit

overview.title: Start with the observation process
overview.body: Review both the amount and location of missingness. The same percentage has different implications when absence is planned, concentrated, or associated with a study condition.

planned_missing.title: Planned absence
planned_missing.body: Ratings omitted by design can be compatible with estimation when the remaining design stays connected and supports the intended comparisons. Document the assignment rule.

unexpected_missing.title: Unexpected missingness
unexpected_missing.body: Missing scores, identifiers, or weights may reflect recording, administration, or participation processes. Locate concentrations before deciding how to proceed.

limits.title: What the audit cannot establish
limits.body: A table of missing counts does not identify a missing-data mechanism. Sensitivity checks or narrower claims may be needed when missingness could change the conclusion.

coverage.title: Check observation coverage and connectedness
coverage.summary: Determine whether the observed design links persons and facet elements strongly enough for the intended comparisons.
coverage.prerequisites: Use mapped long-format data and state which within-run comparisons the study requires.
coverage.computed: The design review summarizes observed combinations and whether the comparison network forms connected components.
coverage.can_show: It can show empty combinations, sparsely observed elements, and comparisons that are disconnected within the observed data.
coverage.cannot_show: Connectedness and dense coverage do not establish population representativeness, construct coverage, or fairness.
coverage.next_check: Inspect sparse rows or columns and confirm that every reported comparison lies within one connected component.
coverage.next_action: Add linking observations when feasible, narrow the comparison, or report disconnected parts separately.
coverage.safe_report: If coverage and connectedness were reviewed, report measures only within the connected portion of the observed design and retain limits on representativeness, construct coverage, and fairness.
coverage.avoid_report: A connected design proves that the sample represents the target population.
coverage.search_alias: coverage; connectedness; linking; sparse design; observation network

overview.title: Why design links matter
overview.body: Facet effects are comparable only when observations provide a chain of links among the relevant persons and elements. Coverage should be judged against the planned claim.

observed_coverage.title: Observed combinations
observed_coverage.body: Review which person-by-facet combinations are present, sparse, or empty. Large structured gaps deserve attention even when the overall row count is high.

connectedness.title: Connected comparison network
connectedness.body: A connected component provides an observed path linking its elements. Measures from separate components do not share an empirically supported within-run comparison.

limits.title: Coverage is not representativeness
limits.body: This check concerns the observed design. It does not show that persons, tasks, raters, or occasions adequately represent a broader population or construct.

large_analysis.title: Adjust an analysis that exceeds current capacity
large_analysis.summary: Preserve the research task while reducing work that cannot be run safely in the current environment.
large_analysis.prerequisites: Know which observations, facets, diagnostics, and outputs are essential to the primary question.
large_analysis.computed: Before estimation, the application compares the requested workload with the capacity available for the current run.
large_analysis.can_show: It can show that the request is too large to execute safely here and which scope choices can be reconsidered.
large_analysis.cannot_show: A capacity limit says nothing about the data, model fit, or substantive result.
large_analysis.next_check: Separate essential estimation from optional diagnostics and large output preparation.
large_analysis.next_action: Reduce the data or optional analysis scope, then review the revised request before running it.
large_analysis.safe_report: If the capacity stop was confirmed, report that the requested analysis was not completed in this session; document any later scope change and do not report a result for the stopped attempt.
large_analysis.avoid_report: The analysis failed because the model or data were invalid.
large_analysis.search_alias: large analysis; resource limit; reduce scope; run capacity

overview.title: A run-capacity boundary
overview.body: The warning protects the application from an unsafe workload. It occurs before a scientific result is created and should not be interpreted as model evidence.

retained_state.title: Confirm what is still shown
retained_state.body: Check whether the input, mapping, and selected settings are still shown before changing scope. Record every change so it is not mistaken for the original analysis request.

safe_scope.title: Reduce scope without changing the question
safe_scope.body: Begin with optional diagnostics, figures, or unused facets. If observations must be reduced, define the rule from the study question and document the resulting population and claim.

estimation_failed.title: Recover when estimation does not finish
estimation_failed.summary: Check the visible input and settings, identify the next reversible check, and avoid treating an unfinished run as a result.
estimation_failed.prerequisites: Keep the data and settings used for the attempt available for review.
estimation_failed.computed: The application records that no finished estimate was produced and presents a bounded recovery route.
estimation_failed.can_show: It can show the stage that needs review and direct you to relevant data, design, category, anchor, or estimation settings.
estimation_failed.cannot_show: An unfinished run cannot support parameter interpretation or a substantive conclusion.
estimation_failed.next_check: Review the displayed problem category, then inspect the named input or setting before trying again.
estimation_failed.next_action: Make one documented change, rerun, and confirm that a finished result and its diagnostics are available.
estimation_failed.safe_report: Estimation did not finish under the stated settings; no parameter result from that attempt was interpreted.
estimation_failed.avoid_report: The failed run showed that the hypothesis was false.
estimation_failed.search_alias: estimation failed; run did not finish; recovery; troubleshooting

overview.title: No finished result was created
overview.body: Treat the event as a workflow problem. Keep the attempted settings visible so the next change is reviewable and does not silently alter the research question.

preserved_state.title: Confirm the visible state
preserved_state.body: Check the input, column mapping, selected settings, and any earlier results that are still shown. This guidance does not by itself confirm that application state was retained.

next_check.title: Choose the next check
next_check.body: Follow the problem-specific action first: review format, coverage, score categories, anchors, or estimation settings. Change one source of difficulty at a time.

nonconvergence.title: Interpret and address nonconvergence
nonconvergence.summary: Understand why an unfinished optimization limits interpretation and which evidence to inspect before rerunning.
nonconvergence.prerequisites: Retain the attempted model, estimation settings, data audit, and convergence summary.
nonconvergence.computed: The estimator evaluates whether parameter updates and the objective have met the stated stopping criteria.
nonconvergence.can_show: It can show that the stopping criteria were not met and provide convergence diagnostics for the attempt.
nonconvergence.cannot_show: Nonconvergence does not show that the construct is absent, the theory is false, or a particular element is defective.
nonconvergence.next_check: Review design connectedness, sparse elements, score categories, constraints, and estimation settings.
nonconvergence.next_action: Address a supported cause, rerun with the change documented, and interpret results only after convergence evidence is satisfactory.
nonconvergence.safe_report: Estimation did not converge under the reported settings, so parameter estimates from that attempt were not interpreted.
nonconvergence.avoid_report: The model was disproved because estimation did not converge.
nonconvergence.search_alias: nonconvergence; convergence check; iterations; estimation stopping

overview.title: Why convergence comes first
overview.body: Parameter tables can look complete even when estimation has not stabilized. Review convergence before fit, measures, interactions, or reporting.

meaning.title: What nonconvergence means
meaning.body: The estimation procedure stopped without satisfying its stated stability criteria. Estimates may still be changing or depend strongly on the stopping point.

does_not_mean.title: What it does not mean
does_not_mean.body: Nonconvergence is not a substantive finding. It may arise from the observed design, sparse categories, constraints, starting conditions, or requested model complexity.

next_check.title: A bounded recovery sequence
next_check.body: Confirm connectedness and category support, inspect extreme or sparse elements, review constraints, then reconsider estimation settings. Record each change and its rationale.

unexpected.title: Recover from an unexpected application problem
unexpected.summary: Pause interpretation, use reversible checks, and retain the support reference if the same problem continues.
unexpected.prerequisites: Note the action attempted, the visible screen, and the displayed support reference. Do not assume whether inputs, settings, or results were retained.
unexpected.computed: This notice produces no analysis claim. The application assigns a generic problem category and a support reference for troubleshooting.
unexpected.can_show: It can direct you to reversible checks and identify the support reference to include in a problem report.
unexpected.cannot_show: It cannot identify the cause, confirm application state, or establish that an analysis result is valid or invalid.
unexpected.next_check: Inspect what is currently visible, note the attempted action, and retry only the last reversible action once if its effect is clear.
unexpected.next_action: If the problem repeats, stop retrying and copy the support reference into the problem report together with the attempted action.
unexpected.safe_report: If documented, state that the affected step was not completed and that no result from that attempt was interpreted.
unexpected.avoid_report: The application problem proves that the model or data are invalid.
unexpected.search_alias: unexpected problem; application error; support reference; reversible troubleshooting; problem report

overview.title: What this notice means
overview.body: An application step ended unexpectedly. This is a troubleshooting event, not statistical evidence about the model, data, or research question.

first_check.title: First reversible check
first_check.body: Before changing data or settings, inspect the source view and note exactly what action preceded the notice. Retry once only when the action is reversible and the current state is clear.

get_support.title: Use the support reference
get_support.body: Include the displayed support reference, attempted action, screen, and approximate time in the problem report. Do not include raw or identifiable research data unless its disclosure is authorized.

first_read.title: Read results in a safe order
first_read.summary: Check whether interpretation can proceed before opening detailed measures, fit statistics, or figures.
first_read.prerequisites: Use a finished run and keep the study question and requested evidence visible.
first_read.computed: The first-read view organizes convergence, design, fit, category, residual, and interaction evidence by interpretation priority.
first_read.can_show: It can show which evidence is available, which requires caution, and which prerequisite must be addressed first.
first_read.cannot_show: A single status, table, or figure cannot establish the complete measurement argument.
first_read.next_check: Resolve any pause condition first, then inspect the detail that directly supports the study question.
first_read.next_action: Write one next-action note that names the evidence, its limit, and the screen where it can be checked.
first_read.safe_report: Interpretation proceeded only after the required design and estimation checks were reviewed.
first_read.avoid_report: All results are trustworthy because the overview showed no warning.
first_read.search_alias: first read; result priorities; interpretation order; evidence overview

overview.title: Read prerequisites before estimates
overview.body: Begin with convergence and connectedness, then review evidence tied to the claim. Detailed values should not outrun the conditions that make them interpretable.

reading_order.title: Recommended reading order
reading_order.body: Review estimation completion, design links, measures and uncertainty, fit, category functioning, residual structure, differential interactions, and planned sensitivity checks. Stop where a required prerequisite is unmet.

claim_boundaries.title: Carry limitations forward
claim_boundaries.body: A caution or unavailable check remains part of the result. Include it in notes, exports, and reports rather than replacing it with an overall pass label.

measures_targeting.title: Interpret measures and targeting
measures_targeting.summary: Read person and facet locations on the logit scale together with uncertainty, coverage, and the intended comparison.
measures_targeting.prerequisites: Confirm convergence, connectedness, the model orientation, and which facet locations are higher or lower on the reported scale.
measures_targeting.computed: The fitted MFRM estimates person and facet locations, their uncertainty, and graphical summaries on a common logit scale.
measures_targeting.can_show: It can show relative locations, uncertainty, distributional gaps, and how observed facet coverage aligns with person locations.
measures_targeting.cannot_show: A location estimate is not a judgment of a person or element and does not by itself justify a ranking or decision.
measures_targeting.next_check: Compare estimates with uncertainty and observation support, then inspect fit for the elements central to the claim.
measures_targeting.next_action: Describe the relevant contrast in logits, name the reference orientation, and retain uncertainty and design limits.
measures_targeting.safe_report: Reported contrasts are on the fitted logit scale and are accompanied by uncertainty and design context.
measures_targeting.avoid_report: A higher measure proves that a person or element is better.
measures_targeting.search_alias: measures; targeting; Wright map; forest plot; facet distribution; logit

overview.title: Locations on a modeled scale
overview.body: Measures express relative locations under the selected MFRM and constraints. Interpret direction, reference point, uncertainty, and the facet meaning together.

wright_map.title: Wright map
wright_map.body: Compare person and facet distributions on the same logit axis. Gaps suggest regions with limited targeting; extreme locations require uncertainty and observation checks.

ecdf_measures.title: Cumulative measure distribution
ecdf_measures.body: The cumulative curve shows the proportion at or below each location. Steep segments indicate concentration, while flat segments indicate gaps; neither pattern is a quality verdict.

forest_measures.title: Estimate and uncertainty plot
forest_measures.body: Read each estimate with its interval. Overlap is not a formal equivalence test, and small visual rank differences should not be emphasized when uncertainty is substantial.

facet_distribution.title: Distribution within a facet
facet_distribution.body: Review center, spread, sparse tails, and isolated elements within one facet. Distributional width is descriptive and depends on which elements were observed.

limits.title: Limits on measure claims
limits.body: Measures depend on the fitted model, constraints, and observed design. Avoid converting modeled locations into labels about inherent ability, severity, or quality.

fit.title: Interpret Infit, Outfit, and residual fit evidence
fit.summary: Use fit statistics to locate observations or elements for review without turning thresholds into automatic exclusion rules.
fit.prerequisites: Confirm a converged, connected fit and review the observation count and uncertainty relevant to each element.
fit.computed: The application summarizes Infit, Outfit, standardized fit, and residual patterns for the fitted model.
fit.can_show: It can identify responses or elements whose variation differs from model expectations and prioritize follow-up.
fit.cannot_show: A fit value cannot by itself diagnose a cause or require removal of a person, item, task, criterion, or rater.
fit.next_check: Inspect observation support, residual examples, content, scoring conditions, and sensitivity before deciding what a flag means.
fit.next_action: Record the flagged element, the statistic, its observation support, and the substantive review undertaken.
fit.safe_report: If observation support and substantive evidence were reviewed, report fit flags as review signals rather than automatic exclusion decisions.
fit.avoid_report: Elements outside a cutoff were automatically deleted as invalid.
fit.search_alias: Infit; Outfit; fit scatter; standardized fit; residual plot; misfit

overview.title: Fit is a diagnostic, not a verdict
overview.body: Infit emphasizes unexpected responses near an estimated location; Outfit is more sensitive to distant unexpected responses. Read both with sample size and context.

fit_scatter.title: Infit and Outfit scatter
fit_scatter.body: Locate elements that are high on one or both statistics. A point outside a reference band identifies a review priority, not an automatic exclusion.

pathway_map.title: Measure-by-fit pathway
pathway_map.body: Read modeled location and the selected fit statistic together. Infit MnSq is the default (reference 1); approximate ZSTD is optional (reference 0, with ±2 review lines). Clusters can suggest a shared design or scoring condition that deserves inspection.

misfit_ranking.title: Review-priority ranking
misfit_ranking.body: The ranking orders large standardized departures so review can begin efficiently. It does not rank substantive quality, and sparse elements may be unstable.

zstd_distribution.title: Standardized-fit distribution
zstd_distribution.body: Use the distribution to see asymmetry, tails, and concentrations of fit flags. Standardized values can be sensitive to observation count and approximation.

qq_residuals.title: Residual quantile plot
qq_residuals.body: Compare the residual distribution with a reference shape to locate tail departures and asymmetry. The plot is descriptive and is not a pass-fail normality test.

limits.title: No automatic removal
limits.body: Investigate content, data entry, scoring conditions, local dependence, and sensitivity. Any exclusion needs a stated rule and a rerun that shows its effect.

categories.title: Review rating-category functioning
categories.summary: Combine observed use, modeled category probabilities, and threshold locations before changing a rating scale.
categories.prerequisites: Confirm the intended category order, response model, and sufficient observations across relevant persons and facets.
categories.computed: The application summarizes category counts, modeled response probabilities, and threshold locations under the selected model.
categories.can_show: It can show sparse categories, limited dominant regions, and threshold patterns that deserve review.
categories.cannot_show: A sparse or disordered pattern does not by itself prove that a category is poor or should be collapsed.
categories.next_check: Review category wording, scorer use, observation counts, uncertainty, and whether patterns persist across relevant facets.
categories.next_action: If a change is considered, justify it substantively and compare the original and revised specifications.
categories.safe_report: Category functioning was reviewed using observed use, modeled probabilities, thresholds, and the scoring design.
categories.avoid_report: A flagged category was automatically collapsed because the plot failed.
categories.search_alias: rating categories; thresholds; category probabilities; category use; step structure

overview.title: Three complementary views
overview.body: Observed use describes what occurred, probability curves describe the fitted response process, and thresholds describe transitions on the modeled scale. Review them together.

category_probability.title: Category probability curves
category_probability.body: Each curve shows the modeled probability of a category across the latent scale. A category without a clear dominant region warrants review, not automatic deletion.

category_usage.title: Observed category use
category_usage.body: Check counts overall and across relevant facets. Sparse use may reflect category wording, sampling, assignment, or scoring practice.

threshold_map.title: Threshold locations
threshold_map.body: Review threshold order, spacing, and uncertainty under the selected RSM, PCM, or GPCM. Disorder is evidence for investigation rather than a stand-alone decision rule.

limits.title: Category changes require design evidence
limits.body: Collapsing categories changes score meaning and the fitted model. Preserve the original rationale, inspect sensitivity, and document the revised interpretation.

residual_structure.title: Explore residual structure
residual_structure.summary: Use residual PCA as a bounded screen for remaining associations after the modeled dimension and facet effects.
residual_structure.prerequisites: Use a converged fit with enough comparable residual profiles and retain the substantive content labels for interpretation.
residual_structure.computed: Residual PCA summarizes major contrasts in residual associations after the fitted model's expected responses are removed.
residual_structure.can_show: It can identify a residual contrast or cluster that deserves stability and content review.
residual_structure.cannot_show: Residual PCA cannot prove or confirm unidimensionality, and a single eigenvalue is not a dimensionality verdict.
residual_structure.next_check: Inspect loadings, content groupings, observation coverage, and stability across defensible settings or resamples.
residual_structure.next_action: Describe any contrast as exploratory, name its content pattern, and seek corroborating evidence before changing the model.
residual_structure.safe_report: If content and stability evidence were reviewed, report residual PCA as an exploratory screen and retain the boundary that it does not confirm unidimensionality.
residual_structure.avoid_report: Residual PCA proved that the scale is unidimensional.
residual_structure.search_alias: residual PCA; residual contrast; scree plot; local dependence; dimensionality screen

overview.title: A screen after model fitting
overview.body: Residual structure concerns associations left after modeled expectations. It is useful for finding patterns that the primary model may not represent.

residual_pca.title: Read residual PCA
residual_pca.body: Review the leading contrast, loadings, and substantive grouping together. Eigenvalue rules are orientation aids, not proof of a separate dimension or its absence.

limits.title: Why the screen is bounded
limits.body: Results depend on residual construction, missing comparisons, sample composition, and stability. Weak signal does not confirm a single dimension.

next_check.title: Follow up a residual contrast
next_check.body: Check whether high and low loading groups share content, method, rater, task, or administration features, then assess whether the pattern is stable and consequential.

rater_evidence.title: Review rater evidence
rater_evidence.summary: Keep agreement, modeled severity, and differentiation as distinct questions about the observed scoring process.
rater_evidence.prerequisites: Confirm which facet represents raters, that raters are linked through the design, and that observation counts support the comparison.
rater_evidence.computed: The fitted MFRM estimates rater locations, while supporting summaries describe agreement, differentiation, and observation coverage.
rater_evidence.can_show: It can show systematic location differences and patterns that warrant review of scoring conditions or training.
rater_evidence.cannot_show: No single rater indicator establishes accuracy, bias, competence, or fairness.
rater_evidence.next_check: Compare location, uncertainty, agreement, and assigned cases before interpreting a rater pattern.
rater_evidence.next_action: Investigate scoring evidence and design conditions, then document any training, adjudication, or sensitivity step.
rater_evidence.safe_report: If these indicators were reviewed, report rater location, agreement, and differentiation as distinct evidence within the observed design.
rater_evidence.avoid_report: One statistic proved that a rater was inaccurate or biased.
rater_evidence.search_alias: rater severity; agreement; rater separation; scorer evidence; differentiation

overview.title: Separate the rater questions
overview.body: Agreement concerns score similarity, severity concerns modeled location, and differentiation concerns distinguishability. They should not be collapsed into one label.

agreement.title: Agreement evidence
agreement.body: Review exact or weighted agreement in relation to score prevalence, category use, and assignment. High agreement can coexist with limited category use or shared systematic effects.

severity.title: Modeled rater location
severity.body: A higher or lower rater location reflects the fitted scoring tendency under the chosen orientation. Read it with uncertainty, assigned cases, and linking.

differentiation.title: Rater differentiation
differentiation.body: Separation-related summaries ask whether observed rater locations are distinguishable beyond measurement error. They do not establish scoring quality or validity.

limits.title: Avoid person-level verdicts
limits.body: Rater patterns may reflect assignment, rubric interpretation, case mix, sparse data, or local interactions. Follow up with scoring evidence rather than labels.

differential_interaction.title: Review differential and interaction evidence
differential_interaction.summary: Review two distinct screens: local facet-pair interactions under the fitted MFRM and classical group-conditioned DIF. Neither is a fairness verdict, and the screens are not interchangeable.
differential_interaction.prerequisites: Define the comparison groups or facet pair in advance and confirm overlap, sample support, and the direction of each contrast.
differential_interaction.computed: For local facet-pair interactions, the application estimates departures from additive MFRM effects. Separately, classical DIF summarizes group-conditioned item differences after matching on the selected score.
differential_interaction.can_show: It can locate combinations or items whose observed pattern differs from the selected model or matched comparison.
differential_interaction.cannot_show: An interaction or DIF flag cannot by itself establish unfairness, bias, discrimination, or a causal mechanism.
differential_interaction.next_check: Review uncertainty, cell counts, multiple comparisons, content, translation, assignment, and sensitivity to the matching or model choice.
differential_interaction.next_action: Treat flags as review priorities and document corroborating evidence before changing an item, rater, task, or decision rule.
differential_interaction.safe_report: If the stated screen, uncertainty, design, and substantive evidence were reviewed, report local facet-pair interactions and classical DIF separately and identify which one produced each flag.
differential_interaction.avoid_report: A flagged interaction proved that the assessment was unfair.
differential_interaction.search_alias: interaction; bias heatmap; differential item functioning; group difference; fairness review

overview.title: Local difference, bounded conclusion
overview.body: These screens ask whether a local combination departs from an additive or matched expectation. They do not determine why the departure occurred.

bias_heatmap.title: Facet-interaction heatmap
bias_heatmap.body: Inspect the direction, size, uncertainty, and observation count for each facet combination. Sparse or isolated cells require particular caution.

classical_dif.title: Classical DIF screen
classical_dif.body: Compare item performance across defined groups after matching on the selected score. Review effect size, multiplicity, matching quality, and content together.

external_group_design.title: Planning school-group comparisons
external_group_design.body:
First name the comparison. Whether rater R1 scores schools A and B differently is a different question from whether that school difference differs between R1 and R2. A comparison of raters within one school alone does not answer the school-DFF question.

The assignments and model assumptions determine which effects can be estimated separately.

- **The model effects can be separated:** Next check stable estimation and adequate precision. Observations in every count-table cell alone do not establish this.
- **Only some comparisons can be separated:** Name each supported comparison. A difference between raters' school effects may be identifiable even when each rater's own school effect is not.
- **The intended comparison cannot be separated:** Report that the assignment cannot answer the question, not that there is no difference. Do not replace an unidentified difference with zero; review overlap in ratings of students from both schools.

Common recordings may link the scale without identifying school DFF. An assumption-derived value for an unobserved combination does not make that combination observed.

This is study-design guidance. The app does not currently provide estimation, confidence intervals or group response curves for this external-group interaction model. The existing heatmap and classical DIF screen are not substitutes for that analysis.

fairness_boundary.title: Fairness requires broader evidence
fairness_boundary.body: Fairness evaluation also needs construct relevance, opportunity, administration, consequences, and stakeholder context. Statistical flags are one input, not the verdict.

claim_limits.title: Write claims that match the evidence
claim_limits.summary: Separate supported, limited, and unavailable evidence so reports preserve the conditions of interpretation.
claim_limits.prerequisites: Keep the study question, analysis specification, first-read checks, sensitivity results, and intended audience available.
claim_limits.computed: The application organizes evidence availability, limitations, and planned-check stability for reporting review.
claim_limits.can_show: It can show which requested results were produced and which stated limits must accompany them.
claim_limits.cannot_show: It cannot decide the study's substantive claim, validate an assessment, or replace researcher judgment and documentation.
claim_limits.next_check: For each sentence, identify the supporting result, uncertainty, design scope, limitation, and any missing prerequisite.
claim_limits.next_action: Revise broad claims into bounded statements and explicitly mark evidence that is limited or unavailable.
claim_limits.safe_report: The observed result is described for the stated data, model, comparison, and uncertainty, with limitations retained.
claim_limits.search_alias: reporting limits; claim boundary; available evidence; cautious wording; results write-up

overview.title: Claims inherit analysis conditions
overview.body: A report should preserve the population, design, model, estimator, scale direction, uncertainty, and diagnostic limitations that make a result interpretable.

supported.title: Supported evidence
supported.body: Use specific wording that names the estimate or pattern and its scope. A result can be available without supporting a broader causal, validity, or fairness claim.

limited.title: Evidence available with limits
limited.body: State the limitation beside the result, explain its likely consequence, and identify the next check. Do not hide a caution in a distant appendix.

unavailable.title: Evidence not available
unavailable.body: Say that the question was not assessed or could not be assessed under the current design. Absence of evidence is not evidence of no effect or no problem.

wording.title: A bounded sentence pattern
wording.body: Name what was observed, under which model and data, with what uncertainty, and what remains unresolved. Avoid confirmed, proved, valid, fair, or unbiased unless supported beyond this analysis.

privacy.title: Review download contents before sharing
privacy.summary: Check what is included, what is excluded, and whether the prepared material is appropriate for the intended recipient.
privacy.prerequisites: Know the sharing purpose, recipient, consent or governance requirements, and which level of detail is necessary.
privacy.computed: The application prepares selected outputs and a description of included and excluded content.
privacy.can_show: It can show which prepared materials contain person-level, response-level, setting, or aggregate information.
privacy.cannot_show: A contents check cannot guarantee anonymity, confidentiality, consent compliance, or safe onward use.
privacy.next_check: Open the contents review, inspect sensitive tables and free text, and apply the study's disclosure rules.
privacy.next_action: Remove unnecessary detail, choose the appropriate sharing option, and review the prepared material again before sending it.
privacy.safe_report: If the prepared material and governance requirements were reviewed, report what was shared, what was excluded, and which disclosure checks were completed.
privacy.avoid_report: The download is anonymous and safe because the application prepared it.
privacy.search_alias: download privacy; sharing check; included files; excluded data; disclosure review

overview.title: Sharing is a separate decision
overview.body: Preparing a download does not authorize sharing. Match the included detail to the recipient, purpose, consent, and governance context.

included.title: What is included
included.body: Review every selected table, figure, setting, note, and aggregate. Pay particular attention to small groups, uncommon labels, and combinations that could reveal identities.

excluded.title: What is excluded
excluded.body: Confirm that response-level and person-level material is omitted when not needed. Exclusion from one package does not remove copies stored elsewhere.

sharing_check.title: Final sharing check
sharing_check.body: Open the prepared material, verify recipients and purpose, inspect disclosure risk, and retain only the minimum information needed for the research task.

repeat_analysis.title: Save what is needed to repeat an analysis
repeat_analysis.summary: Preserve data provenance, settings, evidence, and limitations so the same analytic decision path can be reconstructed.
repeat_analysis.prerequisites: Identify the prepared input, software version, analysis settings, and evidence needed to support the reported claim.
repeat_analysis.computed: The application can prepare settings, result summaries, and instructions that describe how the analysis was run.
repeat_analysis.can_show: It can show whether saved materials correspond to the displayed analysis and which choices shaped the result.
repeat_analysis.cannot_show: Repeating the same procedure does not independently validate the data, model, implementation, or conclusion.
repeat_analysis.next_check: Confirm that the saved settings, evidence, and limitations refer to the same prepared input and reported result.
repeat_analysis.next_action: Store the minimum reproducibility materials with the report and document any later change as a new analysis.
repeat_analysis.safe_report: If input provenance, settings, software version, procedure, and saved evidence were verified, report that these materials permit the stated analysis to be rerun; do not call that independent validation.
repeat_analysis.avoid_report: The result is valid because the same procedure can be repeated.
repeat_analysis.search_alias: repeat analysis; reproducibility; saved settings; analysis provenance; rerun

overview.title: Repeat the decision path
overview.body: Useful reproducibility material explains which prepared data, settings, and evidence produced the report, not merely how to press the run control.

settings.title: Preserve settings and provenance
settings.body: Record the model, estimator, constraints, category structure, anchors, diagnostic requests, software version, and preparation decisions relevant to interpretation.

evidence.title: Preserve supporting evidence
evidence.body: Keep the tables, figures, uncertainty, diagnostics, and sensitivity results cited by the report, together with a clear analysis reference.

limitations.title: Preserve what remains unresolved
limitations.body: Repeatability does not remove missing evidence, design limits, or sensitivity. Carry those limits into every reproduced report.

rsm_pcm_gpcm.title: Choose among RSM, PCM, and GPCM
rsm_pcm_gpcm.summary: Match the response model to the scoring design, category structure, discrimination assumptions, and research purpose.
rsm_pcm_gpcm.prerequisites: Identify the selected step facet, whether its levels share category meanings and step locations, and whether varying discrimination across those levels is substantively defensible.
rsm_pcm_gpcm.computed: The application fits the selected response model within the stated, bounded step-facet structure and reports model-specific category results.
rsm_pcm_gpcm.can_show: It can show parameter estimates, fit, category functioning, and comparative evidence under each supported specification.
rsm_pcm_gpcm.cannot_show: Fit alone cannot determine the correct model or make substantively different category structures interchangeable.
rsm_pcm_gpcm.next_check: Compare the model's constraints with rubric design, category use, parameter stability, and the intended interpretation.
rsm_pcm_gpcm.next_action: State the model choice before interpretation and justify any alternative specification as a sensitivity check.
rsm_pcm_gpcm.safe_report: If the scoring design, selected step facet, model assumptions, and completed diagnostics were reviewed, report the selected response model and the checks used to support that choice.
rsm_pcm_gpcm.avoid_report: The most flexible or best-fitting model was automatically the correct model.
rsm_pcm_gpcm.search_alias: RSM; PCM; GPCM; response model; rating scale; partial credit

overview.title: Model choice encodes scoring assumptions
overview.body: MFRM separates person and facet effects, while the response model specifies how ordered categories behave. Choose constraints that match the rubric and intended score meaning.

rsm.title: Rating Scale Model (RSM)
rsm.body: RSM uses one common category-step structure across all levels of the selected step facet. It suits designs where those levels are intended to share category meanings and step locations.

pcm.title: Partial Credit Model (PCM)
pcm.body: PCM allows category-step locations to vary across levels of the selected step facet while holding discrimination fixed. It suits designs with level-specific category transitions under Rasch-family discrimination constraints.

gpcm.title: Generalized Partial Credit Model (GPCM)
gpcm.body: In this app's bounded GPCM, levels of the selected step facet can have their own category-step locations and discrimination. Discrimination parameters are relative within that facet under a geometric-mean-one constraint; they are not absolute quality scores. This flexibility requires sufficient information.

choice_boundary.title: A comparison does not choose the purpose
choice_boundary.body: Use fit and sensitivity as evidence, but keep design intent, identifiability, parsimony, and interpretability in the decision. Models answer different constrained questions.

jmle_mml.title: Choose between JMLE and MML
jmle_mml.summary: Select an estimator according to the parameter target, person-distribution assumptions, sample and design, and reporting purpose.
jmle_mml.prerequisites: Specify the response model, parameter constraints, intended person inference, and whether a population distribution is part of the analysis.
jmle_mml.computed: JMLE estimates person and facet parameters jointly; MML integrates over a specified person distribution while estimating structural parameters.
jmle_mml.can_show: It can show estimator-specific parameter results, convergence evidence, uncertainty, and sensitivity under supported settings.
jmle_mml.cannot_show: Neither estimator is universally preferable, and agreement between them does not establish validity.
jmle_mml.next_check: Review convergence, parameter target, sample and design support, person-distribution assumptions, and sensitivity to defensible settings.
jmle_mml.next_action: Justify the primary estimator from the research purpose and treat the alternative as a planned sensitivity analysis when appropriate.
jmle_mml.safe_report: If the parameter target, assumptions, convergence, and planned sensitivity evidence were reviewed, report the selected estimator and those completed checks.
jmle_mml.avoid_report: One estimator is always more accurate than the other.
jmle_mml.search_alias: JMLE; MML; estimation method; marginal likelihood; joint likelihood; person distribution

overview.title: Different estimation targets
overview.body: JMLE and MML use different treatments of person parameters. Interpret estimates, uncertainty, and small-sample behavior in relation to that choice.

jmle.title: Joint maximum likelihood estimation (JMLE)
jmle.body: JMLE estimates person and facet parameters jointly under the selected constraints. Because the number of person parameters grows with the sample, estimates can retain small-sample bias; sparse designs can add instability. Review sample and design support rather than treating JMLE as automatically unbiased.

mml.title: Marginal maximum likelihood estimation (MML)
mml.body: MML integrates over a specified person distribution while estimating structural parameters. Conclusions depend on distributional assumptions and numerical integration.

person_distribution_sd.title: Person-distribution standard deviation
person_distribution_sd.body: Under MML, the standard deviation sets or estimates population spread on the latent scale. Review whether it is fixed or estimated, its uncertainty, and sensitivity to distributional form.

choice_boundary.title: Estimator choice is purpose-dependent
choice_boundary.body: Compare convergence, bias considerations, uncertainty, distributional assumptions, and the intended parameter interpretation. Do not select solely from one fit value.

glossary.title: Measurement and workflow glossary
glossary.summary: Look up terms and abbreviations, including cautions for interpreting results.
glossary.prerequisites: No fitted result is required; use the study and screen context to select the intended meaning.
glossary.computed: Displays definitions and related explanations; it does not run an analysis.
glossary.can_show: It can connect plain task language with formal measurement terms and point to related guidance.
glossary.cannot_show: A term label or definition cannot establish that a condition holds in the current analysis.
glossary.next_check: Open the related Help topic and compare the definition with the current model, design, and screen.
glossary.next_action: Use the reviewed term in notes and retain its stated boundary when reporting.
glossary.safe_report: The term is used according to its reviewed definition and the conditions stated for this analysis.
glossary.avoid_report: The presence of a term in the output proves the associated conclusion.

overview.title: Look up an unfamiliar term
overview.body: Look up unfamiliar terms and abbreviations used in the app. For example, standard error and posterior standard deviation both concern uncertainty but describe different quantities. Read the definition together with the related Help topic.

search.title: Search by term or research task
search.body: Use acronyms, full names, or task phrases. Open the related topic when a definition depends on the response model, estimator, design, or diagnostic.

concept_boundaries.title: Definitions are not findings
concept_boundaries.body: Each concept includes a statement it must not imply. Carry that boundary into interpretation rather than using the label as evidence.

writing_essay.label: Writing essay (30×4×2×4, 960 obs)
writing_essay.short: A small, fully crossed writing-assessment example.
writing_essay.description: 30 persons × 4 raters × 2 tasks × 4 criteria, scored in 6 categories. Start with First Read, then follow Check next to inspect measures, fit and the Wright map. The data are synthetic; a successful run does not establish validity for a real assessment.

large_writing_pca.label: Large-scale writing (120×4×2×3, 2,880 obs)
large_writing_pca.short: A larger example with a deliberately severe rater.
large_writing_pca.description: 120 persons × 4 raters × 2 tasks × 3 criteria, scored in 6 categories. Inspect rater severity and residual PCA. Severity is a modeled main effect: a severe rater need not misfit or produce a second dimension. Interpret PCA with its stability checks and item content, not a single eigenvalue cutoff.

speaking_test.label: L2 speaking (80×3×3×5, 3,600 obs)
speaking_test.short: Speaking assessment with five analytic criteria.
speaking_test.description: 80 persons × 3 raters × 3 tasks × 5 criteria, scored in 5 categories. Compare criterion difficulty, category use and fit. Different criterion difficulties alone do not justify PCM or GPCM; those models add criterion-specific threshold spacing or discrimination. Use them only when those differences address the analysis question.

clinical_osce.label: Clinical OSCE (60×4×5×3, 3,600 obs)
clinical_osce.short: Five clinical stations and a four-category rubric.
clinical_osce.description: 60 persons × 4 raters × 5 stations × 3 competencies. The synthetic person distribution is narrow and station difficulty varies. Inspect person separation together with standard errors, coverage and fit. Low separation alone is not evidence of model failure; a narrow rater severity range does not guarantee good fit.

writing_with_missing.label: Writing with missing (80×4×2×3, ~1,632 obs)
writing_with_missing.short: About 15% of response rows removed uniformly at random (MCAR).
writing_with_missing.description: The full synthetic design has 80 persons × 4 raters × 2 tasks × 3 criteria (1,920 rows); about 15% of rows are removed independently of their values. This is MCAR, a special case of MAR. Removed rows are absent, not blank cells, so the app cannot infer the deletion rate from the file alone. Check coverage and connectivity. Random deletion reduces information and does not remove finite-sample estimation bias or guarantee finite estimates.

music_peer_rating.label: Music peer-rating (120×2 cyclic×2×4, 1,920 obs)
music_peer_rating.short: Cyclic peer assessment with a sparse Person × Rater graph.
music_peer_rating.description: 120 participants each rate two peers on 2 pieces × 4 criteria. Person and Rater IDs refer to the same participants but represent different model roles. Inspect connectedness, score coverage and uncertainty. A connected graph alone does not establish a finite, precise estimate, and this assignment does not provide a reciprocal rating for every pair.

reading_testlet_binary.label: Reading testlet — binary (100×1×6×4, 2,400 obs)
reading_testlet_binary.short: Binary scoring with Person, Scorer, Text and Item facets.
reading_testlet_binary.description: 100 persons × 1 scorer × 6 texts × 4 items, with 0 = incorrect and 1 = correct. The current app fits fixed effects for text and item. Inspect residual PCA and item content for possible dependence within a text; PCA is a screen, not a testlet diagnosis. This release does not offer a testlet random-effects estimator or a Stan-generator workflow. If dependence is plausible, reconsider the model with appropriate methods outside this workflow before interpreting uncertainty.

two_school_linking.label: Two schools, common recordings (360 ratings)
two_school_linking.short: Link two schools through ten jointly rated recordings.
two_school_linking.description: Each school has 20 students and two raters. All four raters also score 10 common reference recordings. Each person supplies one recording on the same speaking task, scored on three criteria from 0 to 4: 360 ratings in total. These are synthetic data with illustrative parameter values, not observations from real schools. Open the lesson above the input preview to follow joint calibration and learn how it differs from fixing anchors. See the [FACETS equating guidance](https://www.winsteps.com/facetman64/equating.htm).
two_school_linking.guide_title: Lesson: compare two schools using common recordings
two_school_linking.guide:
**Question: can we compare performances after accounting for rater severity?**
The common recordings connect the two rating panels. This is an example of **joint calibration**: estimate both schools together, without supplying fixed logit values.

**1. Read one row.** A row is one rater's score for one recording on one criterion. `A01`–`A20` are school A students; `B01`–`B20` are school B students. `C01`–`C10` are reference performances, excluded from either school's student summary. There is one person per recording and one shared speaking task. Keep the same `C` ID for the same recording at both schools; do not give different performances the same ID.

| Recordings | Raters | Ratings |
|---|---|---:|
| 20 school A students | A_R1, A_R2 | 120 |
| 20 school B students | B_R1, B_R2 | 120 |
| 10 common references | All four | 120 |

Each rater scores three criteria: Fluency, Clarity and Organization. Retain each individual score; do not average raters first. The generator uses RSM, the same ability distribution for both schools and differing rater severities. A realized sample need not have equal school means.

**2. Run together.** Use Guided defaults (RSM/JMLE), check Person and Score, then Run this analysis. Rater and Criterion are the facets. Task has only one level and is automatically excluded; task difficulty differences cannot be estimated here. Leave fixed and group anchors empty. Constraining the two school means to be equal would remove the very difference you want to examine. Do not add School as a facet nested within Person and Rater.

**3. Check before comparing.** Start with First Read and Check next: inspect interpretation holds, rating connectivity, fit and category use. Use the same rubric and scoring conditions for the common recordings, spanning the performance range of interest. Ten references are an example, not a sufficient-number rule. Removing all common recordings disconnects the Person–Rater design even though the criterion names still match.

**Review criterion-specific rater patterns too.** After fitting, use Open the DFF plot and reading guide below this lesson to reach Diagnostics → Bias/Interaction. The default pair is Rater × Criterion. If only another pair is available, select Rater and Criterion in the analysis settings and explicitly rerun. Open the reading guide and questions beside the plot. No combination-specific bias is deliberately added to this example; sampling variation can still produce different cell estimates. Dark cells are not known true DFF. Local students are rated only by their own school's raters, so this plot does not establish school-specific differential treatment.

Use the count table and group CSV below to inspect cross-school assignments. The CSV has one row per person and leaves School blank for C01–C10: these recordings link the calibration but are not members of either student group. The file supports assignment review; it is not a recommendation to run school-comparison tests.

**4. Read and report.** In the estimates and Wright map, a larger Person logit means higher modeled performance; a larger Rater logit means greater severity. Inspect fit alongside severity. Describe A and B using their student estimates, excluding C references. A mean difference is descriptive: this app does not provide a validated school-mean contrast interval or a causal school-effect estimate. Individual SEs do not by themselves give the SE of that difference.

Open Report & Export for the basic report and add your study-specific explanation. A report should state the shared task and rubric, rating assignment, reference selection, joint RSM/JMLE calibration, constraints, fit and any interpretation holds. Include estimates with qualified uncertainty and fit, plus a Wright map when useful. Do not report that equivalence was proven merely because estimation completed.

**5. Reuse a scale later.** Fixed anchoring is a separate workflow: reuse vetted measures from an earlier calibration for unchanged reference performances. Review the scale's origin, task and criterion compatibility, fit and reference stability before fixing values. Zero deviation from a fixed anchor only confirms the imposed constraint; it does not demonstrate stability. Current SEs do not propagate uncertainty in externally estimated anchor values.

Further reading: [FACETS equating](https://www.winsteps.com/facetman64/equating.htm), [anchor specifications](https://www.winsteps.com/facetman64/labels.htm), and [nested facets](https://www.winsteps.com/facetman64/nested.htm).

metric_notes.fit: Infit and Outfit are mean-square fit statistics (MnSq), with model expectation 1. Underfit (>1) means more unexplained variation than expected; overfit (<1) means less. These are not ability or rater-quality scores. The review flags use separate thresholds; do not exclude a person or rater on this statistic alone.
metric_notes.reliability: Strata (H) = (4G+1)/3 is a conceptual index of distinguishable levels, derived from separation G, not an observed group count or a grouping rule. H = 3 does not establish three actual groups or their cut scores. Reliability here concerns differentiation, not inter-rater agreement; low rater separation can also reflect imprecision.
metric_notes.fit_title: Infit, Outfit and underfit: definitions and next steps
metric_notes.reliability_title: Strata and separation: definitions and next steps
metric_notes.fit_details:
### What the numbers describe

Let r be observed score minus expected score, V the model-predicted score variance, and w the observation weight (1 when unweighted). **Outfit = Σ(w r²/V) / Σw**; **Infit = Σ(w r²) / Σ(w V)**. Infit weights standardized squared residuals by V; Outfit is more sensitive to unexpected observations with small V.

**MnSq = 1 is the model expectation**, not proof that every response matches its prediction. Underfit means excess variation, not low ability. Overfit means less variation, not superior performance or proof of copying.

### Definition versus review flag

A value of 1.2 is above the expectation but remains inside this app’s review band. The unrounded values determine flags: **<0.50** overfit review; **0.50–1.50 inclusive** inside the band; **>1.50–2.00 inclusive** underfit review; **>2.00** priority underfit review. A row uses the more concerning of its available Infit/Outfit values. Missing values are not evidence of fit.

**ZSTD** is an approximate standardized fit statistic, sensitive to observation count and the selected degrees-of-freedom convention. A small absolute value does not prove fit; a large one does not establish a cause.

### Before making a decision

Check the original ratings, observation count, assignment and rubric. For example, a piano judge’s high Outfit can prompt a review of a few surprising ratings; it does not establish unfair judging. Record the substantive reason for any correction or exclusion, and compare justified alternatives.

Definition and reference bands: [FACETS 4: element fit](https://www.winsteps.com/facetman64/table7.htm), [diagnosing misfit](https://www.winsteps.com/facetman64/diagnosingmisfit.htm). The bands are review aids, not universal decision cutoffs.
metric_notes.reliability_details:
### What Strata describes

**H = (4G+1)/3** summarizes spread relative to measurement error under distribution and precision assumptions. H can be fractional or exceed the number of observed elements. **G = 2 gives H = 3**, but does not locate cut scores or demonstrate that the sample contains three groups. Do not round H to assign students, pianists or skaters to ranks or award groups.

### How this app calculates it

For SE-based measures, SD is the sample SD (denominator n−1), RMSE = √mean(SE²), adjusted SD = √max(SD²−RMSE², 0), and **G = adjusted SD / RMSE**. **Reliability = G²/(1+G²)**. G = 0 produces H = 1/3 algebraically; it is not evidence of a fraction of a group. Unavailable values stay unavailable.

For MML person EAP estimates, the app instead uses **G = SD(EAP) / √mean(posterior SD²)** and empirical reliability = Var(EAP) / [Var(EAP) + mean(posterior SD²)]. Posterior SD is not a sampling SE. These EAP summaries are not directly equivalent to FACETS separation indices.

### Before making a decision

Inspect the distribution and uncertainty of the estimates, the number of ratings, and the rating design. Low rater separation may mean similar severity or insufficient precision; it does not establish agreement or interchangeability. Interpretation holds also apply to Strata.

Definition: [FACETS 4: reliability, separation and Strata](https://www.winsteps.com/facetman64/reliability.htm). Check population/sample SD and Model/Real SE conventions before comparing software outputs.

report_faq.title: Reading the results: four questions and answers
report_faq.intro: Start with the Notes beside the tables and figures. These answers explain the terms; they do not establish that a diagnostic was run. Any interpretation hold in this report still applies.
report_faq.references_caption: Sources for these answers are listed below. The downloaded report includes the English Q&A and references.
report_faq.overfit_question: 1. In speech assessment, is rater similarity or overfit good or bad?
report_faq.overfit_answer:
**Similar severity is not the same as overfit.** Similar severity estimates can be desirable when raters are meant to apply the same standard. Overfit means Infit or Outfit mean square (MnSq) is below 1: residual variation is smaller than the model expects. Small departures from 1 can occur by chance; low values alone establish neither accurate scoring nor misconduct (Linacre, n.d.-a).

For English speeches, compare severity estimates and their uncertainty separately from fit. To assess agreement, compare independent ratings of the same performances. Low rater separation reliability means limited evidence of distinguishable severity differences; it does not demonstrate agreement (Linacre, n.d.-c).

**What to check:** If MnSq is unusually low, inspect the original ratings, category use and scoring procedure. Repeated scores, halo effects across criteria, or ratings made jointly rather than independently are possible explanations to investigate, not conclusions from the statistic. Do not remove a rater solely for overfit. Report the fit values, review criterion and findings from the review.
report_faq.wright_question: 3. What does a larger logit on the Wright map mean?
report_faq.wright_answer:
**Read the facet direction before judging the size.** With the usual coding, a higher person measure means a greater tendency to receive higher scores, after accounting for the other facets. It means better performance only when higher category codes represent better performance.

For a negatively oriented rater facet, a larger estimate means greater severity; for a negatively oriented task facet, greater difficulty. Both reduce expected scores with other parameters held fixed. For a positively oriented facet the direction reverses: a larger rater estimate indicates greater leniency. Check the configured direction and score coding (Linacre, n.d.-b).

**Example:** On the same calibration with a negatively oriented rater facet, a judge at +1 logit is more severe than one at -1 logit. This is a difference of 2 logits, not 2 raw score points. Zero is a chosen reference, not zero ability. Read uncertainty and fit alongside the positions; compare separate analyses only after establishing a common linked scale. A map alone does not determine a pass mark or competition ranking.
report_faq.bias_question: 4. What does “bias” mean in bias analysis?
report_faq.bias_answer:
**Here, bias means a specific interaction beyond the overall facet effects.** A speech rater might be more severe on one task than expected from that rater’s overall severity and the task’s difficulty. Being generally strict is an overall rater effect, not by itself this kind of bias. An interaction can reflect rubric interpretation, assignment patterns or substantive differences; it is not proof of intent or unfair discrimination (Linacre, n.d.-d; Myford & Wolfe, 2003).

In this application, **Bias Size** is a logit adjustment to the model’s score tendency while the calibration is held fixed. A positive value raises expected scores; a negative value lowers them. Do not read it automatically as a positive or negative severity contrast: parameter definitions and directions can differ between programs.

**Current limit and next step:** Bias/no-bias conclusions remain withheld in this application because validation of interaction tests and intervals is pending. Retained technical values do not remove that limit. Review cell counts, missingness, shared performances and the rubric. A missing flag or a nonsignificant result does not establish fairness; document the evidence and what remains unresolved.
report_faq.pcm_rsm_question: 2. How do PCM and RSM differ, and which data suit them?
report_faq.pcm_rsm_answer:
**The difference is whether category-step structures are shared.** Both models analyze ordered category scores. The rating scale model (RSM) assumes a common step structure after accounting for differences in item or facet locations. It is a candidate when the same rubric and category progression are defensible across the relevant tasks or criteria. Shared thresholds do not mean equally spaced thresholds (Andrich, 1978).

**The partial credit model (PCM) allows the step structure to vary.** For example, the relative difficulty of receiving 2 rather than 1, or 3 rather than 2, may differ across criteria. In this application, PCM estimates separate step structures for levels of the selected step facet. A speech or piano rubric whose criteria have different category progressions can motivate this model (Masters, 1982).

**How to choose:** Use the rubric and study design, then inspect category counts, probability curves, fit and residuals. The same 0–5 labels do not establish RSM; different criterion names do not establish PCM. RSM uses fewer parameters; PCM generally needs more observations to estimate its additional thresholds reliably. Sparse categories can make either model unstable. Neither model alone establishes that one trait is sufficient. Report the rationale and follow any model-comparison hold shown by the app.
